items.title: Agent Plugins
items.text:
Turn a useful workflow into a reusable agent capability—and check whether it actually helps.

A good instruction is not yet a dependable capability. People must be able to find it, understand its boundaries, install its supporting files, and judge its results. Agent Plugins provides focused creators for that journey.

items.title: What will you learn?
items.text:
You will learn to choose the right kind of capability, create a first Skill, validate its structure, and compare its behavior with a baseline. Maintainers can then learn how verified source becomes an installable distribution.

flowchart LR
    A[Useful workflow] --> B[Choose a creator]
    B --> C[Create a focused capability]
    C --> D[Validate its structure]
    D --> E[Evaluate paired results]
    E --> F[Review before sharing]

For example, “summarize meeting notes” is still broad. “Read one Markdown file and separate recorded decisions from open questions, without inventing facts” gives the author and reviewer an observable outcome.

items.title: Choose your learning path
items.text:
Your situation Start here Then continue New to Skills and plugins Concepts Getting started Ready to make something small First Skill tutorial Evaluate and improve Already know your goal Choose and use creators Reference Want to change this repository Contributing Upstream development guidance

The tutorial is a guided learning exercise. The how-to pages solve specific tasks. The reference is a lookup aid, not a substitute for the walkthrough.

items.title: What is included?
items.text:
Four creators cover Skills, custom agents, lifecycle hooks, and complete plugins. A fifth Skill, Script Packaging, helps design contained executable resources. Choose by responsibility, not by whichever creator name looks familiar.

The recorded repository documentation lists distribution 0.5.0, the portable Agent Plugins 1.0.0 target, and verified host integration with Goose 1.47.0. These are recorded verification values, not a claim about the latest releases. Open file formats do not guarantee equivalent behavior in every host.

items.title: Install from the distribution; learn from upstream
items.text:
The installation URL is https://github.com/servierhub/agent-plugins.git. The ServierHub distribution and the personal upstream source have distinct roles. Deeper documentation links on this site point to upstream develop; ready-to-install Skill links point to the distribution's main.

Follow Getting started for installation. Git-installed creators require Node.js 22+, but no build, npm dependency installation, or Bun installation. Native release archives are a separate installation mode.

items.title: What counts as success?
items.text:
You can explain the capability's purpose, inspect its generated files, distinguish validation from evaluation, and identify missing evidence. A blocked or inconclusive evaluation is useful information—not a pass.

Review executable behavior and never package secrets. Goose is the verified reference host; compatibility with other hosts requires testing their own implementation.

Next: Understand the concepts or install and check discovery.

items.title: Concepts: purpose before packaging
items.text: Start with the outcome you want the agent to achieve. Only then decide which files and host features are necessary.

items.title: Skill, custom agent, hook, or plugin?
items.text:
Concept Purpose Example Boundary Skill Reuse a focused workflow and its resources Summarize decisions from Markdown Agent Skills format; discovery depends on the host Custom agent Give a delegated role its own instructions A reviewer focused on authentication risks Recorded Goose custom-agent contract Lifecycle hook React to an event in the host lifecycle Record selected tool activity Executable, host-specific behavior Plugin Distribute capabilities together A release-note Skill plus integrations Portable core plus explicit host adapters Script packaging Make executable resources installable A contained TypeScript CLI runtime Packaging guidance, not release approval

A plugin is not simply a bigger Skill. It introduces package-level discovery, configuration, integration, and release concerns. A custom agent is not a place to declare MCP transports or credentials.

items.title: Three questions, three kinds of evidence
items.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Capability candidate] --> B[Format validation: does it conform?]
    A --> C[Trigger evaluation: is it selected?]
    A --> D[Behavioral evaluation: does it help?]
    B --> E[Review evidence and limits]
    C --> E
    D --> E
    E --> F[Revise or make a justified decision]

Validation checks files and contracts. Trigger evaluation checks whether the host selects a Skill for appropriate requests. Behavioral evaluation compares outcomes when a capability is used. Passing one does not establish the others.

For a summary Skill, a positive trigger case might ask to extract decisions from meeting notes; a negative case might ask for a translation only. A behavioral case checks whether the summary actually preserves decisions and avoids inventing answers.

items.title: Portable format is not portable execution
items.text:
The supported portable plugin target is Agent Plugins 1.0.0. Its core uses a required root plugin.json, optional immediate Skill directories under skills/, and optional root mcp.json. Portable 1.0.0 does not define hooks or custom agents.

The recorded Goose adapter describes additional behavior. For example, the audited Goose plugin MCP loader defaults to .mcp.json, not portable mcp.json, and supports stdio conversion rather than all portable remote transports. Let Plugin Creator validate the portable artifact and the intended host separately; do not infer runtime support from a valid schema.

The recorded 1.1.0 draft is inactive, not a supported generation target. See the portable conformance reference and Goose adapter snapshot.

items.title: Progressive disclosure and containment
items.text:
A Skill starts with SKILL.md; supporting references, scripts, and assets belong inside that Skill's directory. Keep the central workflow short and directly link deeper details where needed. Copying only SKILL.md can omit essential resources.

For this distribution, Git-installed executable creators contain compiled JavaScript and production dependencies in their own runtime/. They must not depend on another Skill or root authoring sources at runtime. Native archives replace that Node payload with platform executables; the two payload modes must not be mixed.

items.title: Scope and trust
items.text:
Project-local installation affects a project; user installation exposes a capability more widely. Goose uses .agents/skills/ and ~/.agents/skills/ for standalone Skills. These paths are an installation convention, not the Agent Skills file-format specification.

Instructions, hooks, and scripts can influence commands and file writes. A manifest does not sandbox a process. Review side effects, external requirements, credential handling, and failure behavior before enabling a capability.

items.title: Check your understanding
items.text:
If a plugin validates but no paired runs exist, its behavior is not evaluated. If a Skill works in one Goose scenario, that does not establish another host's compatibility. If a required reviewer is unavailable, keep the decision blocked, not passed.

Next: Getting started, creator selection, or evaluation.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: The goal of a contribution is a reviewable change with reproducible evidence—not a hand-edited installation tree. Think of develop as the workshop and main as the packaged product.

items.title: Understand the branch lifecycle
items.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Focused feature branch] --> B[Reviewed PR to develop]
    B --> C[Authoritative develop source]
    C --> D[Exact-SHA CI and current authorization]
    D --> E[Reverify source, approval, and main]
    E --> F[Allowlisted production projection]
    F --> G[Fast-forward publication to main]

Feature PRs target develop. That branch contains sources, tests, configuration, vendored dependencies, and generated Skill runtime mirrors. main is the generated Git-installable distribution; it deliberately excludes root authoring apps and build tooling.

A same-repository develop → main PR is a promotion review request, not a source merge. Publication creates a generated-tree commit with previous main as its sole parent, pushes normally, and closes the PR without merging. Never merge develop into main or force-push production.

The policy and publication permissions are repository-specific. The upstream migration is recorded; ServierHub publication has separate permissions and migration considerations. Do not change credentials or remotes to work around them.

items.title: Prepare a scoped contribution
items.text:
1. Read AGENTS.md, the affected creator guide, and existing issues.
  2. Follow the repository's Beads guidance for tracking. bd prime explains the workflow; bd ready shows available work. Explicit user or orchestrator restrictions still take precedence.
  3. Inspect your checkout and preserve existing changes. Start a focused feature branch from develop.
  4. State acceptance criteria and the exact evidence needed in the PR.

For a fresh upstream checkout:

git clone --branch develop https://github.com/bioinfornatics/agent-plugins.git
cd agent-plugins
git switch -c feature/my-change

This is contributor source setup, not the ServierHub installation command. Creating a branch does not authorize an automated agent to commit, push, or synchronize tracker remotes.

items.title: Restore development dependencies
items.text:
Contributor prerequisites include Node.js 22+, pinned Bun 1.3.12, Git, and Beads. Full integration verification needs the recorded Goose 1.47.0 executable and applicable browser tooling. Native release packaging has additional archive tools and platform runners.

In a fresh development checkout:

node scripts/prepare-development.mjs

This restores the verified vendored dependency closure offline, without network installation or lifecycle scripts. It refuses to overwrite existing development modules. Inspect an existing checkout rather than deleting dependencies blindly. Dependency upgrades require deliberate lockfile and vendored-closure changes.

items.title: Edit sources, then regenerate deliverables
items.text:
Location Purpose apps/<creator>-cli/ TypeScript sources, tests, generated dist/ contracts/ Shared contracts and compatibility fixtures skills/<name>/ Independently installable instructions and resources skills/<name>/runtime/ Generated compiled implementation and production dependencies config/skill-runtimes/ Versioned app-to-Skill mapping config/reproducibility/ Versioned source closure and platform rules vendor/ Verified offline build dependencies .artifacts/ Disposable previews and build outputs

Fix implementation sources, not generated runtime files. For a focused Skill Creator change:

(cd apps/skill-creator-cli && npm run build && npm test)
npm run build:skill-runtimes
npm run check:skill-runtime-dist-drift

Changes to shared contracts or other apps need their own builds and fixture refreshes before runtime generation. Follow the complete build order in CONTRIBUTING.md. Retain regenerated mirrors with the source candidate; CI rebuilds and rejects committed-output drift. The clean rebuild command is a drift gate, not a way to bless stale outputs.

items.title: Verify the exact candidate
items.text:
Command Main scope npm run test:distribution Distribution structure and adoption documentation npm run test:production Projection, containment, provenance, promotion guards npm run test:production-ci Routine production profile and creator/integration checks npm test Full developer suite, including applicable packaging checks npm run test:reproducibility-build Isolated clean-source build reproducibility npm run test:reproducibility Exhaustive isolated verification

Before release, run each creator app's npm run build && npm test and the required root gates. Automated tests must not mutate live ~/.agents directories. Missing tools or behavioral evidence are limits, not passes.

Routine CI verifies the exact source head SHA, not a synthetic merge tree. It restores dependencies, clean-builds, checks output coherence, tests the production profile, and checks deterministic projection and isolated Git installation/update. Five-platform release packaging is deferred from routine CI; scheduled/manual exhaustive and tagged-release workflows cover their applicable packaging checks.

items.title: Preview without publishing
items.text:
Use a destination that does not already exist:

node scripts/production.mjs project .artifacts/production-preview
node scripts/production.mjs verify .artifacts/production-preview
node scripts/production.mjs smoke .artifacts/production-preview

Success check: the preview passes the applicable projection and smoke checks and contains self-contained Skills rather than root authoring dependencies. This preview is not publication or approval. A recorded HEAD from an uncommitted working tree does not prove that edits are committed; release verification needs a clean exact-SHA candidate.

items.title: Respect promotion and authorization limits
items.text:
Normal promotion requires independent current-SHA approval and successful exact-head CI, followed by source and authorization reverification. Stale approvals, self-approval, forks, or outstanding change requests do not qualify. A personal repository owner may explicitly authorize owner-manual promotion with exact source/main bindings; that is owner authorization, not independent review.

Workflow guards are not configured branch protection. Required checks and publisher permissions must be configured separately, and review checks are not atomic with GitHub reviews. If publication succeeds but PR closure fails, inspect provenance before retrying. Follow the branch migration and rollback policy rather than improvising publication commands.

items.title: Documentation, cleanup, and handoff
items.text:
Keep user explanations separate from contributor tooling. The production README source is docs/production-README.md; links from production to deeper development files need full develop URLs. Add new canonical sources to the reproducibility manifest as required by repository policy.

Skill metadata and instructions remain English, with concise third-person descriptions and SKILL.md at most 500 lines. Move deeper detail into directly linked references. Refresh vendored snapshots before changing a public format contract, preserve evaluation evidence, and keep every Skill independently installable. Bilingual site prose does not change Skill authoring contracts.

Routine cleanup preserves Skill runtimes, vendor dependencies, evaluation evidence, and .agents/ content. Do not use broad deletion commands in their place. At handoff, report changed files, exact checks, limitations, tracker status when applicable, and proposed next actions. Commit, push, and Dolt remote synchronization require explicit authority under the conservative policy.

Further reading: Full contributing guide, Reference, and evaluation guidance.

items.title: Getting started
items.text: The goal is to make a creator discoverable and confirm it can help without changing files. Creating a Skill comes next.

items.title: 1. Choose your installation mode
items.text:
Use Goose for the integration recorded as verified by this repository (1.47.0). Other hosts require their own documented installation and compatibility checks.

Mode You need You do not need Git plugin installation Host, Git installation capability, Node.js 22+ Build, Bun, npm dependency installation Whole standalone Skill directory Host with standalone Skill discovery; Node.js 22+ for the Git payload Root repository tooling Tagged native archive Matching OS/CPU archive and verified checksum Node.js or npm dependencies

Only install code and instructions you trust. Automatic updates trade manual control for convenience; choose deliberately.

items.title: 2. Install the Git distribution
items.text:
Check Node.js:

node --version

Then install:

goose plugin install https://github.com/servierhub/agent-plugins.git

This is the ServierHub distribution, not the personal upstream development checkout. Installed plugins live under ~/.agents/plugins/<name>/; project-local plugins may live under .agents/plugins/<name>/.

items.title: 3. Check discovery without writing files
items.text:
Start a new Goose session and ask:

Use agent-plugins:skill-creator to explain what information you need to create a Skill. Do not modify any files yet.

Success check: the creator resolves and asks about the intended outcome, activation conditions, workflow, constraints, and evaluation needs. Discovery alone does not prove that a generated Skill will behave correctly.

Next: work through the first Skill tutorial in a scratch project.

items.title: 4. Understand updates and alternatives
items.text:
To opt into automatic updates, use this installation command instead:

goose plugin install --auto-update https://github.com/servierhub/agent-plugins.git

To update a Git-backed plugin on demand:

goose plugin update agent-plugins

For a standalone Skill on Linux or macOS, copy the whole directory:

git clone https://github.com/servierhub/agent-plugins.git
cd agent-plugins
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills
cp -R skills/skill-creator ~/.agents/skills/skill-creator

Use skill-creator rather than the plugin-qualified name for that standalone installation. Goose discovers project Skills in .agents/skills/ and global Skills in ~/.agents/skills/; check other hosts separately. The installable Skill tree includes supporting files that must remain together.

Native archives are selected manually; Goose's Git installer does not select them automatically. Download the matching archive and SHA256SUMS from the same tagged release, verify before extraction, and never mix Node and native payloads. Follow the release installation guide; check which repository actually publishes the release you intend to use. Manually copied installations have separate updates.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Symptom What to check Creator not found New session; qualified name for plugin, plain name for standalone Git creator does not launch Node.js 22+ and complete Skill directory including runtime/ Missing runtime dependencies Reinstall the complete distribution; do not repair with npm install Validation failure Follow the named file or field diagnostic; do not bypass it Evaluation blocked Supply the missing execution, grading, test, or review evidence Wrong native version Check PATH, OS/architecture, and old wrappers

Report reproducible defects to the upstream issue tracker, not a separate ServierHub queue. Include installation mode, versions, command, diagnostic, and a minimal non-sensitive reproduction.

Next: First Skill tutorial or creator selection.

items.title: Reference
items.text: Use this page to look up recorded versions, paths, command boundaries, and source documents. For a guided introduction, start with Concepts and Getting started.

items.title: Recorded targets and requirements
items.text:
Item Recorded value or rule Distribution 0.5.0 Portable plugin target Agent Plugins 1.0.0 1.1.0 snapshot Working Draft, inactive; not a supported target Verified host integration Goose 1.47.0, not a claim about latest Goose Git-installed creator runtime Node.js 22+; compiled code and production dependencies included Native release runtime Platform-specific Bun executable; no Node.js requirement Contributor tooling Node.js 22+ and pinned Bun 1.3.12; routine CI uses Node.js 22.22.2 License CeCILL-C

Verification of Goose does not establish compatibility with another host. See the recorded Goose plugin reference for revision-specific details.

items.title: Names and installation surfaces
items.text:
Surface Project User Notes Standalone Skills .agents/skills/ ~/.agents/skills/ Use a plain creator name Goose custom agents .agents/agents/ ~/.agents/agents/ Separate from bundled plugin Skills Plugins .agents/plugins/<name>/ ~/.agents/plugins/<name>/ Plugin Skills use qualified names Repository instructions AGENTS.md Host-dependent Guidance, not an installed plugin component

Qualified creator names are agent-plugins:skill-creator, agent-plugins:agent-creator, agent-plugins:hook-creator, agent-plugins:plugin-creator, and agent-plugins:plugin-script-packaging. Creator selection explains their scopes.

The portable Skill file contract centers on the Skill directory and SKILL.md; the .agents/skills paths are a discovery convention. Do not assume every host uses them.

items.title: Portable plugin files and host boundary
items.text:
File or directory Meaning Root plugin.json Required portable manifest skills/<name>/SKILL.md Optional immediate bundled Skill; resources remain inside that Skill Root mcp.json Optional portable MCP declaration with explicit transport Namespaced Goose extension Repository-defined host adapter, not portable execution semantics Root hooks/hooks.json Legacy Goose input, not the new-output hook layout Bundled agents/ Not portable 1.0.0 custom-agent installation; not auto-discovered by audited Goose

Portable MCP supports the recorded stdio, streamable-http, and sse variants. The audited Goose plugin loader defaults to .mcp.json and converts stdio declarations. Explicit selection of a portable stdio-only ./mcp.json may work under the recorded contract; do not infer remote transport support or allow duplicate activation. Consult portable conformance before migration.

items.title: Stable command entrypoints
items.text:
The executable creators expose skill-creator, agent-creator, hook-creator, and plugin-creator. Native archives inject these into each Skill's scripts/ directory, with .exe on Windows. The Git distribution uses contained Node launchers; installation does not imply a shell PATH entry. Use the appropriate installed launcher or native executable, not internal source paths.

Operation Documented example Skill format validation skill-creator validate /path/to/skill Skill authoring audit skill-creator audit /path/to/skill --format json Evaluation preview skill-creator full-eval /path/to/skill --workspace /path/to/workspace --dry-run Static evaluation review skill-creator review /path/to/iteration-workspace --static review.html Portable plugin loading checks plugin-creator validate /path/to/plugin --mode portable-load --format json Strict plugin authoring checks plugin-creator validate /path/to/plugin --mode strict-authoring --format json Agent definition checks agent-creator validate /path/to/agent.md --require-filename-match Hook checks hook-creator validate /path/to/plugin

For Skill Creator, Agent Creator, and Plugin Creator, recorded exit codes are 0 success, 1 failure, 2 invalid usage, 3 blocked. Hook Creator's README documents 0, 1, and 2; do not assume all creators have identical command or exit-code contracts. Each command's --help is the lookup entrypoint. The CLI is not a substitute for a configured runner, model, grader, or actual human review.

items.title: Native archive lookup
items.text:
Platform Asset Linux x86-64 agent-plugins-creators-linux-x64.tar.gz Linux ARM64 agent-plugins-creators-linux-arm64.tar.gz macOS Intel agent-plugins-creators-darwin-x64.tar.gz macOS Apple silicon agent-plugins-creators-darwin-arm64.tar.gz Windows x86-64 agent-plugins-creators-win32-x64.tar.gz

Verify the archive against SHA256SUMS from the same release before extraction. A native archive contains four complete creator Skill trees, not a claim that every repository Skill is included. Never combine archives or add old Node runtime payloads. See RELEASES.md for checksum commands and PATH checks. Asset availability and publication are repository-specific; confirm the release you download.

items.title: Source documents and installable resources
items.text:
These are recorded repository references, not freshly verified upstream host documentation:

  • User README, CONTRIBUTING.md, and branch migration policy.
  • Creator guides: Skill, Agent, Hook, Plugin, Script Packaging.
  • Vendored host snapshots: Goose plugin format, custom agents, hooks.
  • Installable distribution: manifest on main and Skills on main.
  • Public specifications: Agent Skills and Agent Plugins.
  • Defects and development discussion: personal upstream issues.

items.title: Evidence and safety vocabulary
items.text:
Validated means the applicable structural checks passed. Evaluated requires behavioral evidence. Blocked names an unmet prerequisite. Inconclusive means the available evidence does not resolve the claim. Approved requires the applicable authorization; passing tests alone does not authorize production.

No manifest sandboxes executable code. Keep resources contained, document external dependencies, and never distribute secrets. For a decision workflow, use Evaluate and improve.

items.title: Choose and use the creators
items.text: Choose the owner of your requested outcome before asking for implementation. A clear request names the outcome, destination, constraints, and success criteria.

items.title: Select the smallest appropriate scope
items.text:
You want to… Creator Responsibility Create, audit, improve, or evaluate one Skill agent-plugins:skill-creator Skill instructions, resources, and evaluation Create or improve a delegated persona agent-plugins:agent-creator Goose custom-agent definitions Add or test a lifecycle hook agent-plugins:hook-creator Hook behavior, scripts, and specialist checks Assemble, migrate, validate, or package a plugin agent-plugins:plugin-creator Manifest, MCP, component coordination, integration, packaging Design executable packaging agent-plugins:plugin-script-packaging Language-aware runtime and launcher guidance

Use unqualified names such as skill-creator for standalone installations. Plugin Creator coordinates specialists; it does not replace their authoring logic. Script Packaging advises on executable design; Plugin Creator owns final whole-plugin validation and release approval.

items.title: Create or improve one Skill
items.text:
Use agent-plugins:skill-creator to create .agents/skills/api-review. Review an OpenAPI diff for breaking changes and produce a concise Markdown report. Keep the Skill portable, add realistic evaluation cases, validate the result, and show the files and missing evidence.

Check: the output is a focused Skill directory, not an agent definition or a complete plugin. Confirm its activation conditions, limits, and supporting resource paths. For an existing Skill, preserve its baseline before requesting changes. See the first Skill tutorial and evaluation guide.

items.title: Create a custom agent
items.text:
Use agent-plugins:agent-creator to create a project-local code-reviewer agent focused on correctness, security, and regression tests. Explain its delegation boundaries, validate its definition, and show it before installation. Do not change enabled extensions or package a plugin.

Check: custom-agent output belongs under the documented .agents/agents/ surface, not in a Skill directory. Evaluation should compare isolated delegated tasks with a neutral delegated baseline or an earlier agent version—not convert the agent into a Skill.

A custom agent may use MCP extensions already enabled in its Goose session. It cannot declare MCP transport, command, environment, or credentials in its own definition. Route that configuration to Plugin Creator. A bundled plugin agents/ directory is not automatically installed or discovered as custom agents in the audited Goose revision. Consult the Agent Creator guide for the recorded contract rather than copying a frontmatter template here.

items.title: Add a lifecycle hook safely
items.text:
Use agent-plugins:hook-creator to add a lifecycle hook to ./my-plugin that records selected shell tool activity. Use a plugin-relative script, explain its side effects and failure behavior, validate the matcher and referenced files, and show the result before enabling it.

Check: begin with a valid plugin manifest; review what data is recorded and where it goes. Handler tests and host integration evidence are distinct. Blocking behavior, such as a PreToolUse policy, requires explicit failure-mode review.

The Hook Creator README contains a legacy root hooks/hooks.json layout. The current Goose adapter reference specifies namespaced extension output for new hooks. Do not copy the legacy layout into new output or combine both forms; have the creators validate migration explicitly. Hooks are not portable Agent Plugins 1.0.0 core behavior.

items.title: Assemble a complete plugin
items.text:
Use agent-plugins:plugin-creator to create ./release-assistant with a portable Skill for drafting release notes. Validate it in portable-load and strict-authoring modes, separate host-specific behavior, and show the package before making an archive.

Check: plugin.json is valid, bundled Skills are contained, MCP declarations are validated against both format and host, and integration evidence covers changed behavior. Packaging does not substitute for evaluation or approval.

Portable root mcp.json and Goose MCP loading differ. Do not guess precedence or remote transport support; use the Plugin Creator guide and the recorded adapter checks.

items.title: Package executable resources
items.text:
Use agent-plugins:plugin-script-packaging to plan a contained TypeScript CLI for this Skill, including the Git-installation runtime and native-release boundary. Explain dependencies and verification before changing launchers. Leave final plugin validation and release approval to Plugin Creator.

TypeScript is the default guidance branch; Rust and Python have conditional branches. This is not a blanket promise of bundled runtimes for every language or host. Read the Script Packaging guide.

items.title: Before accepting the result
items.text:
Ask for changed files, exact validation outcomes, execution evidence, unresolved risks, and a next action. Never include secrets or silently enable executable behavior. If a capability or review is unavailable, keep it blocked rather than treating static checks as a behavioral pass.

Next: Evaluate and improve or Reference.

items.title: Evaluate and improve from evidence
items.text: The purpose of evaluation is to make a decision you can justify: keep, revise, or reject a capability. It is not to generate a favorable score. Start with realistic tasks and an explicit baseline.

items.title: 1. Separate the questions
items.text:
Format validation asks whether files conform. Trigger evaluation asks whether a Skill is selected appropriately. Behavioral evaluation asks whether using it helps on the tested tasks. Human review decides whether the evidence and trade-offs are acceptable.

flowchart TD
    A[Freeze candidate, baseline, and scenarios] --> B[Validate and audit]
    B --> C[Run paired scenarios]
    C --> D[Grade outputs using evidence]
    D --> E[Aggregate and generate review]
    E --> F{Required evidence complete?}
    F -->|No| G[Report blocked and supply missing evidence]
    G --> F
    F -->|Yes| H[Human review and verification]
    H --> I[Keep, revise, or reject]

items.title: 2. Choose cases that can expose failure
items.text:
For the summary tutorial, include explicit decisions, discussion only, an unresolved question, and a document with no relevant content. Assertions should distinguish accurate extraction from plausible invention.

Example criterion: “The answer preserves the question about who reviews the examples without naming a reviewer.” This is more useful than “The answer is good.” Keep deterministic checks and qualitative review questions distinct, and use the same fixtures for both variants.

Freeze the candidate, evaluation plan, and baseline before running. Compare with_skill with old_skill or without_skill; do not compare unrelated tasks or silently change the conditions between variants.

items.title: 3. Request paired evaluation
items.text:
Use agent-plugins:skill-creator to evaluate .agents/skills/markdown-summary against a without-Skill baseline on the same realistic scenarios. Preserve paired outputs, grade every run using explicit evidence, aggregate the benchmark, and generate a static HTML review. Identify regressions and trade-offs. Report missing execution, grading, timing, tests, or human review as blocked; recommend only evidence-backed changes.

For shell workflows, use the installed stable executable, not a source dist/ path. The following paths are placeholders:

skill-creator full-eval /path/to/skill --workspace /path/to/workspace --dry-run
skill-creator full-eval /path/to/skill --workspace /path/to/workspace --execute --model <model>

Choose a real configured model; execution may consume provider resources and needs a supported runner. Dry-run is non-mutating. Without --execute, the orchestrator does not invoke an LLM and reports the evidence needed to continue. Completed artifacts are preserved on rerun or resume.

The recorded run profiles are fast, standard, and release, with 1, 3, and 5 deterministic counterbalanced pairs per scenario. Repeated profiles require sufficient evaluation budget. One pair is a diagnostic, not convincing evidence of stable gains. See the Skill Creator guide for precise orchestration requirements.

items.title: 4. Inspect artifacts, not just a headline
items.text:
Look for paired outputs and grading, benchmark.json, benchmark.md, a static report such as review.html, and a source-bound receipt.json. The receipt binds the Skill, plan, execution evidence, benchmark, review, and analysis to hashes; changed inputs require fresh applicable evidence.

Read individual failures and disagreements. Check which timing or resource observations are actually available before claiming efficiency. Missing metrics are not zeros. A strong average can hide a material regression.

items.title: 5. Resolve review checkpoints honestly
items.text:
Skill Creator uses exit code 3 for blocked verification or execution. A human-review checkpoint may mean automated phases completed but a real decision is still needed—not that evaluation failed or passed.

After actual review and tests have passed, the documented resume form is:

skill-creator full-eval /path/to/skill --workspace /path/to/workspace --resume --human-review pass --tests-status pass

Do not supply pass flags as a substitute for doing the review or tests. Record their provenance and limits. Unavailable runner, model, grader, or reviewer capability must remain explicit; simulated execution is not behavioral approval.

items.title: 6. Improve without losing the baseline
items.text:
Preserve failed outputs and previous versions. Propose a bounded change tied to a failure, rerun both variants where required, and look for new regressions. The evidence-loop workflow records proposed, challenged, approved, and measured revisions in a separate ledger rather than silently editing the source Skill.

You may conclude “better on these cases,” “regressed on this case,” or “inconclusive.” Do not generalize beyond scenario coverage or confuse successful format validation with improvement.

items.title: Evaluate other capability types
items.text:
Custom agents use isolated delegation and neutral or earlier-agent baselines. Hook evaluation combines handler tests, side-effect review, and applicable host integration. Whole-plugin evaluation coordinates component receipts with routing, trigger overlap, hook effects, and cross-component handoffs.

Plugin Creator's full-eval orchestrator does not run or simulate an LLM. It requests missing specialist and integration evidence and stops blocked until requirements are met. Its workspace must be a proper subdirectory of the plugin's evaluations/ directory. See Plugin Creator evaluation and typed component evidence.

items.title: Success check and limits
items.text:
A useful handoff identifies the exact candidate and baseline, scenarios, artifacts, verdict, regressions, missing evidence, and next action. Validation, evaluation, packaging, and production authorization remain distinct. No evaluation can establish untested host compatibility or guarantee correctness on all future inputs.

Next: Reference or Contributing.

items.title: Tutorial: create your first Skill
items.text: You will turn one small, observable task into a portable Skill: read a Markdown file and report its decisions and open questions. The purpose is to learn the authoring and review loop, not to prove a production capability in one example.

items.title: Before you begin
items.text: Complete Getting started. Work in a scratch project where you authorize file creation. Use a plugin-qualified creator name after plugin installation, or the plain skill-creator name after standalone installation. No external API or custom executable is needed for this exercise.

items.title: 1. Define what good output means
items.text:
Use this small fixture as meeting.md in your scratch project:

# Release planning
- Decision: publish the migration guide before the release.
- Decision: keep the existing configuration keys for this release.
- Open question: who will review the examples?
- Discussion: a new dashboard might be useful later.

Expected behavior: two decisions, one open question, and no invented reviewer. The dashboard discussion is not a decision. This distinction makes the task testable.

items.title: 2. Ask for a focused Skill
items.text:
Use agent-plugins:skill-creator to create .agents/skills/markdown-summary. It should summarize one Markdown file into key decisions and open questions, without inventing facts or treating discussion as a decision. Write the Skill metadata and instructions in English. Keep it simple and portable, validate it, and show the created files and anything still needing evaluation. Do not add a custom agent, hook, external API, or unnecessary script.

Answer the creator's clarification questions. Specify what to do when a file has no decisions or questions: say that none are recorded, rather than filling the gap.

items.title: 3. Review the generated files
items.text:
Check that .agents/skills/markdown-summary/SKILL.md exists. Read it before use. Its purpose and activation conditions should match the request, and its workflow should explain how to separate explicit decisions, open questions, and other discussion.

Supporting files are optional, not a goal. If any are generated, check that they remain inside the Skill directory and are directly referenced when needed. A short, self-contained workflow may need only SKILL.md.

Ask the creator to explain the validation result. Format conformance and authoring policy are separate checks; neither is evidence of better summaries. Avoid unnecessary complexity to satisfy imaginary requirements.

items.title: 4. Try the fixture
items.text:
In a session where the new project Skill is discoverable, explicitly ask the host to use markdown-summary on meeting.md and return decisions and open questions.

Success check: the answer preserves both decisions, leaves the reviewer question unanswered, and does not promote the dashboard idea into a decision. The agent should not modify the input file.

This is a smoke check, not a paired behavioral evaluation and not a trigger-accuracy study. Explicitly loading a Skill does not show that the host would choose it unaided.

items.title: 5. Add a boundary case
items.text:
Try a second file containing discussion only:

# Ideas
A dashboard could make the release easier to follow.
We might discuss ownership next week.

Success check: the summary reports that no decisions or open questions are explicitly recorded. It should not convert a possible future discussion into a current assignment.

If the behavior is wrong, preserve the output and describe the specific failure before editing the Skill. Add a realistic evaluation case for it instead of merely expanding the instructions.

items.title: 6. Know when to stop
items.text:
You have completed the tutorial when the files are inspectable, validation is reported, and the two smoke checks have recorded outcomes. Report unresolved behavior honestly.

For a claim that the Skill helps, compare it with without_skill or an earlier old_skill version on the same scenarios, with grading and review evidence. Follow Evaluate and improve. Do not package or enable more widely just because one answer looked good.

Continue: Creator selection for other capability types, or the Skill Creator guide for advanced workflows.
